hook: A single-page FBI submission to AARO consisting of a redacted still image captured by a U.S. military sensor system in 2025, showing a small dark circular object to the right of a crosshair reticle against an indistinct mountain or cloud background.
why_it_matters: This submission illustrates the FBI's formal role in the AARO reporting pipeline, contributing sensor imagery from military systems to the all-domain resolution process. The chain-of-custody note that imagery was 'altered with redactions before being submitted to AARO' is significant — it means AARO itself received a degraded version of the original military capture. The absence of an accompanying mission report, combined with an uncalibrated system clock, leaves the image largely without verifiable context.
key_findings: The still image was derived from a U.S. military sensor system and submitted by the FBI to AARO as a formal UAP report in 2025.
The original imagery was redacted before reaching AARO, meaning the reviewing office did not receive the unaltered source material.
No accompanying mission report was provided, stripping the image of operational context such as altitude, speed, or observer platform.
The timestamp embedded in the image is acknowledged to be incorrect due to the system clock not being properly set, undermining date-of-observation reliability.

The operator who captured the image was unable to positively identify the object, and the image shows a small, dark, circular shape near the center reticle of what appears to be a targeting or surveillance display.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: AARO is explicitly named as the recipient of this FBI-submitted UAP image, placing this document directly within the formal post-2022 government UAP reporting and resolution framework.

The image originates from an unspecified U.S. military sensor system, and Wright-Patterson has historically been a hub for military UAP imagery analysis, though no direct connection is stated in this document.

The reported location is the Western United States, a broad region that overlaps with restricted military airspace historically associated with classified test and surveillance operations, though no specific site is named.
